_meta.description: Legal knowledge base for ComplyRisk AI audit engine. UAE-focused: UAE PDPL (Federal Decree-Law No. 45/2021) and DIFC DPL No. 5/2020 are primary; GDPR is secondary for EU-expansion exposure.
_meta.verified: 2026-09-25 via Exa research against primary sources

sources.cnil_cookie_enforcement: CNIL SAN-2021-023/024 (2021-12-31): Google EUR 150M, Facebook EUR 60M + EUR 100k/day injunction; Conseil d'Etat upheld Google EUR 100M (2020 case) on 2022-01-31

critical_caveats: UAE PDPL has NO published fine schedule: Art. 26 delegates all penalty amounts to a Cabinet decision that has NOT been issued. Executive Regulations were still unpublished as of 2025-01-06 (DLA Piper). ALL 'default_exposure_calc' AED figures in this file are ANALYST ESTIMATES for demo purposes, not statutory penalties. penalty_framework.basis='estimate' marks them.

UAE PDPL Art. 13 is 'Right to Obtain Information', NOT child data protection. The decree has no dedicated children article; guardian-consent duties derive from consent rules (Art. 5-6). Child age threshold is not set in the decree; UAE law-firm guidance reads 'child' as under 18.
UAE PDPL in-force practical enforcement remains limited; UAE Data Office is the supervisory authority ('Bureau').

DIFC DPL Schedule 2 caps administrative fines at USD 10k-100k per contravention (Art. 62(2)); uncapped 'general fines' under Art. 62(3). DPO-related breaches ~USD 25k, transfer breaches ~USD 50k per Schedule 2.
GDPR Art. 8 default child consent age is 16; Member States may lower to 13 (not below).
_meta.exposure_model: exposure = default_exposure_calc * jev_noul_probability; turnover-based rules scale with user-provided annual_revenue (default USD 5M)

rules.law: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45/2021 on Personal Data Protection (PDPL)
rules.check_description: Confirm processing adheres to PDPL lawful bases (Art. 5) and consent conditions (Art. 6): consent must be provable, clear/simple/unambiguous, and withdrawal must be easy with the right stated in the consent request itself.
rules.noul_assertion: The privacy policy fails to state valid consent conditions under UAE PDPL — no provable affirmative consent, or omits the right to withdraw consent easily at any time.

penalty_framework.note: PDPL Art. 26 delegates fines to unpublished Cabinet decision; figure is analyst estimate.

rules.evidence: UAE PDPL Art. 6(1): controller must prove consent; consent request must state right to withdraw; withdrawal allowed 'at any time'.
rules.remediation: Add a UAE PDPL consent clause: affirmative opt-in, stated right to withdraw at any time, and a working withdrawal channel (privacy portal or dedicated email).

rules.law: UAE PDPL / DIFC Data Protection Law No. 5 of 2020
rules.check_description: Check whether a DPO appointment and its accessible contact details are published. PDPL Art. 10-11 require a DPO where processing involves sensitive data or large-scale/systematic monitoring; DIFC DPL requires DPO appointment and annual assessment for high-risk processing.
rules.noul_assertion: The document lacks contact details for an appointed Data Protection Officer (DPO) or local representative accessible within the UAE/DIFC jurisdiction.
rules.evidence: DIFC enforcement stats 2025: 717 preliminary notices + 273 decision notices issued — active enforcement regime, unlike UAE mainland.
rules.remediation: Publish DPO contact (e.g., dpo@company.ae) and the UAE representative for regulatory correspondence; DIFC entities: file Annual Assessment.

rules.law: UAE PDPL Art. 22-23 / DIFC DPL Art. 26-28 / GDPR Art. 44-49
rules.check_description: Audit cross-border transfer disclosures: PDPL Art. 22 permits transfers only to adequate jurisdictions or under safeguards (Art. 23: contracts/SCCs, BCRs, consent, legal claims). DIFC Art. 26-27 impose adequacy/SCC requirements; Art. 28 adds government-data-sharing safeguards.
rules.noul_assertion: The privacy policy describes international data transfers without naming adequate jurisdictions, Standard Contractual Clauses, or other UAE PDPL Art. 23 / DIFC Art. 27 safeguards.
rules.evidence: PDPL Art. 13(1)(g) separately requires telling data subjects which safeguards protect cross-border processing — missing transfer clause also breaches information duty.
rules.remediation: Name hosting jurisdictions, identify sub-processors, and cite the specific Art. 23 safeguard (DIFC-issued SCCs exist — 'DIFC Abbreviated SCCs 2023').

rules.check_description: Confirm documented commitments to notify the UAE Data Office ('Bureau') of breaches and inform affected data subjects where the breach threatens privacy/confidentiality — PDPL Art. 9 sets no fixed hour deadline (period set by Executive Regulations); GDPR requires 72h.
rules.noul_assertion: The policy contains no data breach incident-response clause — no commitment to notify the UAE Data Office or affected users within defined timeframes after unauthorized access.

penalty_framework.uae_note: UAE fines unpublished (Art. 26); GDPR ceiling applies for EU-facing exposure

rules.evidence: PDPL Art. 9(1)-(4): controller must notify Bureau per Executive-Regulation period; Bureau verifies cause and imposes Art. 26 penalties on proven violation.
rules.remediation: Document breach protocol: immediate Bureau notification on becoming aware, user notification for high-risk breaches, named incident owner.

rules.check_description: Verify the policy gives UAE data subjects actionable procedures for: obtaining information (Art. 13), erasure (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), restriction (Art. 17), objection incl. automated processing/profiling objection (Art. 18). A mere list of rights without a working request channel fails.
rules.noul_assertion: The policy omits an actionable procedure (form, email, or portal plus processing timeframe) for data subjects to exercise UAE PDPL rights — erasure, rectification, restriction, objection.
rules.evidence: PDPL Art. 18 grants objection right specifically against automated processing/profiling — overlaps the AI-transparency check.
rules.remediation: Add a 'Your Rights under UAE PDPL' section: named request channel, committed response timeframe, identity-verification steps.

rules.check_description: Check handling of sensitive personal data (health, biometric, genetic, racial/ethnic, religious, political) and children's data: PDPL prohibits sensitive-data processing absent explicit consent or listed exemptions; children require verifiable guardian consent (under-18 per UAE practice; no statutory age in the decree).
rules.noul_assertion: The service processes or may process sensitive categories or minors' data but the policy omits explicit-consent/guardian-consent workflows and states no minimum age.
rules.evidence: No dedicated UAE PDPL child article — correct prior citation of 'Art. 13' (that article is Right to Obtain Information). Guardian consent derives from Art. 5-6 consent conditions.
rules.remediation: State minimum age (18 per UAE practice) with a no-knowing-collection disclaimer; for sensitive data, cite the explicit-consent basis per Art. 5 exemptions.

rules.law: UAE PDPL Art. 13(1)(c) & Art. 18 / GDPR Art. 22
rules.check_description: Confirm disclosure of automated processing/profiling decisions (PDPL Art. 13(1)(c) requires telling subjects about decisions made on automated processing including profiling) and an objection mechanism (Art. 18).
rules.noul_assertion: The policy fails to disclose whether personal data feeds automated decision-making or profiling, and provides no human-review or objection channel for such decisions.
rules.evidence: PDPL Art. 13(1)(c): right to be informed of 'decisions made based on automated processing, including profiling' — unique UAE hook vs GDPR's narrower Art. 22.
rules.remediation: Disclose profiling/automated-decision usage and add an opt-out/human-review request channel.

rules.check_description: Verify a 1-click 'Reject All' mechanism equally prominent to 'Accept All' on the first cookie layer; no pre-ticked boxes; withdrawal as easy as consent (GDPR Art. 7(3)).
rules.noul_assertion: The site or policy fails to provide an equally prominent 1-click 'Reject All' for non-essential cookies, or uses dark patterns such as pre-ticked consent boxes.

penalty_framework.note: CNIL enforced under national ePrivacy transposition (French DPA Art. 82), not GDPR Art. 83 directly — same consent standard, regulator-controlled procedure.

rules.evidence: CNIL 2021-12-31: Google EUR 150M, Facebook EUR 60M for asymmetric reject path (3-5 clicks vs 1) + EUR 100k/day injunction; earlier CNIL 2020: Google EUR 100M, Amazon EUR 35M — upheld by Conseil d'Etat 2022-01-31.
rules.remediation: Add 'Reject All' identical in prominence to 'Accept All' on layer 1; default-uncheck non-essential trackers.

rules.check_description: For EU-facing operations: consent must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous opt-in; provable (Art. 7(1)); withdrawal as easy as granting (Art. 7(3)).
rules.noul_assertion: The privacy documentation permits processing on implied consent, opt-out models, or continued browsing without verifiable affirmative action.
rules.evidence: CNIL redacted decision (2023): EUR 40M fine citing Arts. 7, 12, 13, 15, 17, 26 breaches — consent defects compound with other articles in one action.
rules.remediation: Affirmative opt-in per purpose; record consent proof; withdrawal UI matching opt-in effort.

rules.check_description: For EU-facing services offering information society services to children: consent valid at 16+; below that requires parental-responsibility holder's consent; member states may lower the age to 13 minimum; controller must make reasonable verification efforts.
rules.noul_assertion: The service offers EU-facing features but states no age threshold or parental-consent verification for under-16 users.
rules.evidence: GDPR Art. 8(1): 'at least 16 years old'; MS may lower to >=13. UK lowered to 13; DE/HU/NL kept 16; AT/IT 14.
rules.remediation: State 16+ (or per-market threshold 13-16) for EU users plus verifiable parental-consent flow.

rules.check_description: Confirm a documented commitment to notify the ADGM Commissioner of Data Protection of a personal-data breach without undue delay, and where feasible within 72 hours (s.32(1)); high-risk breaches also require notifying affected data subjects in clear language (s.33).
rules.noul_assertion: The policy contains no breach-notification clause covering regulator notice within 72 hours and data-subject communication for high-risk breaches, as required by ADGM DPR s.32-33.

penalty_framework.note: DPR s.55 caps each Penalty Notice at USD 28M total per contravention set; figure models a mid-severity notice.

rules.evidence: ADGM enforcement is real: Penalty Notice 1/2024 — Okadoc Technologies (registered at 15-122 WeWork, Hub71 Al Khatem Tower — this venue) fined USD 20,000 for data-subject-rights failures; VentureRock Global received a Direction for Security Principle breaches (June 2023).
rules.remediation: Add a breach-response clause: notify the ADGM Office of Data Protection via the Online Registry within 72h of awareness, communicate to data subjects in plain language when high risk, and document delay reasons.

rules.check_description: For ADGM-registered entities: internal data protection policy in place (s.22(2)), cooperation duty with the Commissioner (s.29), DPO designation where required + notification to Commissioner within one month (s.35(4)), and paid Data Protection Fee (fixed penalty for non-payment, s.56).
rules.noul_assertion: The site gives no indication of ADGM registration, a documented internal data-protection policy, DPO designation/contact, or awareness of the ADGM data protection fee obligation.

penalty_framework.note: Okadoc (Hub71 tenant) was fined USD 20k for rights/policy/cooperation breaches — the floor precedent; cap is USD 28M per s.55.

rules.evidence: Okadoc Penalty Notice (May 2024): USD 20,000 for missing internal DP policy + DSAR handling + non-cooperation — the fined entity sits in Hub71 itself, so 'we're small/a startup' is not a defense.
rules.remediation: If ADGM-registered: adopt a written internal DP policy (s.22), complete the ODP DPO assessment and notify appointment within one month (s.35(4)), and keep the annual Data Protection Fee current (s.56 fixed penalty).

rules.check_description: For ADGM-registered controllers: personal data may leave ADGM only to jurisdictions on the ODP adequacy list (all EC-adequate jurisdictions auto-included, s.41(3)(b)), or under appropriate safeguards — ADGM SCCs adopted under s.42(2), BCRs (s.43), approved codes/certification (ss.37/39), or s.44 derogations (explicit consent, contract necessity, vital interests).
rules.noul_assertion: The policy claims or implies transfers outside ADGM/UAE without naming an adequacy basis, ADGM/EU standard contractual clauses, binding corporate rules, or a s.44 derogation.

penalty_framework.note: s.55 cap USD 28M; modeled at mid-tier — unlawful transfers are among the most-fined violation classes in comparable regimes.

rules.evidence: ADGM ODP guidance Part 6: adequacy list mirrors EC decisions; SCCs are the standard safeguard — absence of any transfer clause is a per-se compliance gap for ADGM entities using overseas processors.
rules.remediation: Add a transfer clause naming the mechanism: adequacy jurisdiction list, ADGM SCCs (or EU SCCs + ADGM addendum), or specific s.44 derogation. Map where data actually goes (hosting, processors, analytics).

rules.check_description: PDPL requires controllers/processors to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures — Art. 20 names encryption, pseudonymisation, confidentiality/integrity/resilience of systems, timely restore capability, and ongoing effectiveness testing.
rules.noul_assertion: The policy contains no commitment to technical and organisational security measures (encryption, access control, integrity, testing) for personal data.

penalty_framework.note: PDPL Art. 26 fines set by executive regulations; modeled at UAE mid-tier.

rules.evidence: VentureRock Global (ADGM) received a formal Direction for Security Principle breaches — UAE-regime regulators actively pursue missing security commitments.
rules.remediation: Publish a security-of-processing clause: encryption at rest/in transit, access controls, integrity/availability measures, and periodic effectiveness testing per PDPL Art. 20.
